newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks slip in lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks slip in lower turnover.

text.p: Saudi shares slipped 0.7 percent last week after two weeks of gains, while services and banks continued to dominate trade, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Saturday.
The index ended the week at 165.58 points from 166.75 a week earlier.
Of the 60 companies traded, 16 rose, 36 declined and eight were unchanged.
The services sector accounted for 31 percent of trade, followed by banks, which made up 26 percent of volume, and industrials, with 22 percent.
BFA put turnover in the week at 8.35 million shares worth 1.78 billion riyals from the previous week's 8.58 million shares worth 1.69 billion riyals.
Riyad Bank was the most active share for the second straight week, accounting for 17.6 percent of volume and 22.7 percent of value dealt. Riyad Bank ended the week 1.4 percent lower at 278 riyals.
The week's top gainer was Yanbu Cement, rising 15.6 percent to close at 260 riyals. Saudi Industrial Export continued to plough ahead, adding 11.5 percent to close at 145 riyals.
Arar Electricity was the week's third biggest gainer, rising 10.0 percent to 55 riyals.

Leading decliners was SCECO-Western, which lost 12.4 percent to close at 92 riyals. Makkah Construction and Development Company dipped 10.4 percent, closing at 267 riyals. National agricultural marketing company Thimar dropped 9.4 percent to end the week at 77 riyals. ($1=3.75 riyals)
